# Job Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 424v–425r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_023_page_001.jpg, JOB_023_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Then Job replied:

**2** "My complaint today is still defiant; his heavy hand presses down on me despite my groaning.

**3** If only I knew where to find him — if only I could go to where he dwells!

**4** I would present my case before him and pour out my arguments in full.

**5** I would discover how he would answer me and grasp what he would say.

**6** Would he overpower me with his great strength? No — he would actually listen to me.

**7** There an honest person could reason with him, and I would be cleared once and for all by my judge.

**8** But I go east — he is not there; I go west — I cannot find him.

**9** When he is at work in the north, I catch no glimpse of him; when he turns to the south, I cannot see him.

**10** Yet he knows every step I take; when he has tested me, I will emerge pure as gold.

**11** I have followed closely in his footsteps; I have stayed on his path without veering off.

**12** I have never strayed from what his lips commanded; I have valued the words from his mouth more than my daily food.

**13** But he is unchangeable — who can oppose him? Whatever he desires, he does.

**14** He will carry out the plan he has for me, and he has many more such plans.

**15** That is why I am terrified in his presence; when I think about it, I tremble with fear.

**16** God has drained the courage from my heart; the Almighty has overwhelmed me with dread —

**17** yet it is not the darkness itself that silences me, not the deep gloom that covers my face."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The paradox of verses 10-16:** This chapter captures Job at his most theologically sophisticated. In v.10, he expresses breathtaking confidence — "I will emerge pure as gold." By v.15, that same God terrifies him. This is not a contradiction but a profound insight: the God who refines is also the God who is utterly beyond control. Job's faith and his fear share the same root — God's sovereign freedom.

**Compass directions (vv.8-9):** The Hebrew uses "forward/backward/left/right," which in the ancient orientation (facing east) correspond to east/west/north/south. PNEUMA renders the compass directions directly for modern clarity.

**v.17 — The chapter's final enigma:** Job says his terror comes not from the darkness but from God himself. The deepest darkness is not the suffering but the silence of the one he seeks.

*— PNEUMA*
